body:
>IntenseBeige wrote in message <20001210012035.20894.00004281@ng-fc1.aol.com>...
>>There are records of Ted having been to see a few docs. Several times for
>>depression and also because he feared he had heart problems. He was pretty
>>straight about drugs, alcohol and nicotine; he wasn't the type to get a bottle
>>of pills from anyone besides a doc.

I thought I knew everything about the Unabomber case but the above is news to me!
And there is no real way about knowing his true usage of drugs or alcohol but
his extremely limited budget would seem to preclude it (unless he had a little
marijuana patch in the woods).

>>>"If our society had no social problems at all, the leftists would
>>> have to INVENT problems in order to provide themselves with an excuse
>>> for making a fuss."
>>
>>Pretty unfair critique of leftists, since there *are* and *always have been*
>>real problems that leftists have worked on. I know for a fact that the poor,
>>tired leftists would *love* a break, be we ain't gettin' none.

I HATE leftists almost as much as the Unabomber.  While some people are more
fascinated with the ecological or technological aspects of the essay, I am
most attracted to the parts about Leftism.  He is telling the absolute truth
about their real psychological motives.

>>Here's a funny aside - snowmobiles will no longer be allowed in national parks,
>>within the next two years. A leftist move, of course, the business uber alles
>>right are not happy about this. Do you know TK's position on snowmobiles?

Well, the Unabomber would disapprove of snowmobiles because they are machines.
I don't snowmobile myself but I can't imagine why they should be banned from
national parks.  I am not aware of any significant pollution problems and the
only reason I can see for their ban is the disruption of wildlife.

>>TK's critique sounds like it applies to all kinds of powerful groups with
>>agendas, not just the left.

>>I ask you again to examine ISAIF critically. In doing so, you might find the
>>nuggets worth the effort, and worth the discussion. TK wanted criticism of
>>ISAIF, even asked for it. He didn't just want people to pander to him.

I used to have a copy that I spent an enormous amount of time formatting in a
nice MS-Word format using a pleasant Arial 14 font for easy reading and printed
it out and put it in a nice binder.  Unfortunately, both disk and binder have
disappeared so I have to read it on my computer monitor.  But I will re-read
the essay in its entirety and focus more on the other parts.

Dark Cloud
